audit.whatIsWrong: Five rows disagree with the packet, each contradicting its own why: win[0]='Skill' beside whys[0] 'Level 1 is yours'; win[1]='Jax' beside whys[1] 'Level 2 is even'; win[3]='Skill' beside whys[3] 'Levels 4-5 stay Jax's'; win[5]='Jax' beside whys[5] 'First item is yours'; win[6]='Jax' beside whys[6] 'even to slightly Jax'.
audit.why: Packet chart: Wukong, Skill, Jax, Jax, Skill, Wukong, Skill, matching the jax__wukong mirror. Win rate 51.66% over 604 games.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 3, 5 and 6 flipped in matched full/content pairs; ratings raised to 6/10 on Level 1 and First item.

audit.whatIsWrong: Counter Strike is named as the matchup-defining cooldown in eleven places without ever carrying its number.
audit.why: 17/15/13/11/9s. At rank 1 that is a 17-second hole — the largest and most reliable commit window Wukong gets in this lane, and it halves as he levels, which is exactly why levels 4-5 slip to Jax.
audit.corrected: Written into whys[3] and the ability-interactions box, matching the 17s-to-13s figure the mirror used.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors. (1) spikes[1] claims 'Grandmaster's ult armor/MR is worthless against a fed Wukong burst'. Riot's R text explicitly grants increased Armor and Magic Resist — it is not worthless against physical burst, it is directly aimed at it, and telling a player otherwise invites them to commit into it. (2) 'Stack Counter Strike autos then unload the empowered stun' and 'his stacked Counter Strike' imply the stun itself is empowered by stacking. Riot's text says only that he 'dodges all incoming attacks for a short duration and then quickly counterattacks, stunning all surrounding enemies'.
audit.why: Riot R text: 'Every third consecutive attack deals additional Magic Damage. Additionally, Jax can activate this ability to deal damage around himself and strengthen his resolve, increasing his Armor and Magic Resist for a short duration.' Riot E text as quoted.
audit.corrected: Grandmaster-at-Arms grants armour and MR for a short duration, so open before he presses it rather than into it, and its passive adds magic damage on every third consecutive attack. Counter Strike dodges ALL attacks while active — the window has to be waited out, not traded through.

audit.why: Short trades beat extended ones here: Relentless Assault ramps his attack speed the longer he autos, and the R passive pays out on every third consecutive attack. The page's 'trade in short Q bursts, not extended auto-fights' is right for the right reason.
audit.corrected: Reinforced in wants.foe[2] by naming the third-attack payout rather than a vague 'on-hit scaling'.

audit.whatIsWrong: Same as point 3 — the page's entire trading rule is 'when it is down', with no timer.
audit.why: 17s at rank 1 versus Empower at 7s and Leap Strike at 8s: only Counter Strike is genuinely punishable, and saying so tells the reader which of the three to actually count.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay Jax's — stacked Counter Strike wins any extended trade you take.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay Jax's — Counter Strike drops from 17s to 13s by rank 3.

edits.before: Your R Cyclone knocks him up and disrupts his all-in, and Grandmaster's ult armor/MR is worthless against a fed Wukong burst — this is your best window to flip the lane.
edits.after: Your R Cyclone knocks him up and disrupts his all-in. Grandmaster-at-Arms gives him armour and MR for a short duration, so open before he presses it, not into it.

edits.before: With Eclipse or Black Cleaver online your Q shred and R burst can out-trade his stacked Counter Strike if you dodge the stun-frame with W.
edits.after: With Black Cleaver online your Q shred out-trades him, but Counter Strike dodges ALL attacks while active — never auto into it, wait the window out.

edits.before: Stack Counter Strike autos then unload the empowered stun
edits.after: Dodge your autos with Counter Strike, then stun you

edits.before: Drag you into a long fight where Jax's on-hit scaling wins
edits.after: Drag you long — his R hits magic every third attack

edits.before: Track Jax's Counter Strike: Dodges autos + stuns. Bait it. When it is down — E-Q + R him.
edits.after: Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1: it dodges every attack, then stuns. Bait it, then commit.

notes: The packet flags 'Bait Counter Strike' in wants.you[0] as a probable wrong name — FALSE POSITIVE, that is the correct ability name. The genuinely dangerous line was spikes[1], which told the reader that Grandmaster-at-Arms' 'armor/MR is worthless against a fed Wukong burst'. Riot's text grants exactly that armour and MR, so the page was inviting a player to commit burst into the one button built to eat it. Rewritten to open before he presses it. Also corrected the 'stacked Counter Strike' / 'empowered stun' framing — Riot's text describes dodging all attacks for a duration followed by a stun, with nothing about the stun being empowered by what it dodged. Counter Strike's 17s at rank 1 appeared nowhere despite the ability being named in eleven places; it is now in whys[3] and the interactions box. Level chart: five rows disagreed with the packet and their own whys; flipped to match the jax__wukong mirror.
